name: Pale Russian Blue
lede: Pale Russian Blue is a near-white, grey-blue, the library's lightened variant of [[russian-blue]], the shade named for the Russian Blue cat breed's coat.

sections.title: A modifier on an existing name
sections.body: The library's index records two Ridgway matches here as well: plate XLII, hue 45 (tone f, ISCC-NBS block 184) and a second entry at plate XXXIV, hue 43 (tone f) [1]. The two hues are close enough that the 1955 ISCC-NBS system files both under very pale blue, about 4.2 units away in CIEDE2000 [1]. Measured in LCH it has lightness 79, chroma just 6 and hue 219 degrees, barely tinted, and [[ash]] than to any strong blue [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive, a match appears in 351 of 23,781 paintings, about 1.5 percent, as photographed; the within-painting lens finds it in 255 [2]. That is ahead of 74 percent of our named colors [2]. It plays a light tone in 62 percent of its appearances, almost never a shadow [2]. It peaks in the 1800s, in 154 of 8,345 paintings, 1.8 percent of the 8,345 paintings (154 of them) we have from that century, about 1.6 times the archive's typical rate [2]. Camille Pissarro is its most devoted painter, carrying it in 9 of his 50 archived works, 7.3 times the typical rate, and Alfred Sisley carries it at 6.4 times the archive rate, in 7 of his 50 paintings [2]. It shares canvases more than chance would predict with [[greyish-white]] [2].

questions.q: Pale Russian Blue is built by adding "pale" to which existing color name?
True or false: Pale Russian Blue is almost always a shadow color in our archive.

openers: Camille Pissarro and Alfred Sisley together carry Pale Russian Blue at several times our painting archive's typical rate.

issues: Field notes named a painter (Childe Hassam, 4/13, 19x) and a 'Nepalese paintings' claim that appear nowhere in the cited fieldnotes; the real top painters are Camille Pissarro (9/50, 7.3x) and Alfred Sisley (7/50, 6.4x), and there is no country data at all for this color. The companion color (powder-blue/sky-blue) was also wrong; the real shared-canvas match is Greyish White. Corrected throughout.
